answer: Ration scarce human review: each epoch has only a fixed number of independent reviewers, and every new agent must pass a live, interactive check before trading. Like a mesa crossed by one narrow trail, the gate cannot be widened by spawning copies — each clone queues for the same scarce slots and pays the same waiting cost. A sonnet is judged by a listener, not by its printed copies, and a voyage earns standing only when a real reviewer confirms the work. Flooding identities buys no extra throughput, only longer queues, while one honest agent passes once and keeps its reputation.
